lines_of_business: All lines of business unless noted in Program Exceptions
FEP: follow FEP guidelines (excluded from NIA review)
Medicare Advantage: CMS NCD 240.4.1, NCD 240.4, LCD L38398, L33405, Article A57496
criteria_location: Position Statement (pp.~3-14): a signs/symptoms box, a site-of-service box, then a two-column layout (test name left, criteria right) for HSAT, PSG, titration, split night, repeat testing, MSLT, MWT, actigraphy, CDL, pediatric, hypoglossal nerve stimulation (HGNS) pre/post-implant, and non-covered tests. Frequency limits and required documentation are NOT in the Position Statement but in Reimbursement Information; AHI/ESS definitions are in Definitions.
procedures_covered: Attended PAP titration (95811, pediatric 95783) and APAP unattended titration (E0601)
Testing before/after hypoglossal nerve stimulator implant
Non-covered: overnight oximetry for OSA, acoustic pharyngometry, SNAP <3 channels, cephalometric x-ray for OSA dx, PAP-Nap, etc.

logic.top_level: pathways: one block per test type, each with its own mix of all/any; the HSAT block is 'all of A,B,C,D', PSG is '(A and B) or (A and C) or D'

k_of_n.quote: witnessed apnea during sleep; OR at least one sign/symptom from category A and one sign/symptom from category B
meets the definition of medical necessity when a member presents with (A&B, A&C, or D)

logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: HSAT eligibility is expressed as a negative: 'B. Absence of other comorbid medical conditions or concomitant sleep disorders such as:' followed by ~8 comorbidities and ~6 sleep disorders ('such as' = non-exhaustive). The very same comorbidity list is reused as a POSITIVE criterion for PSG (B), split night (B), titration (C) and repeat titration (2B). A separate Noncovered list gives indications where PSG/HSAT never qualify (insomnia, circadian, RLS, snoring only, asymptomatic, employer-mandated).
logic.initial_vs_repeat: Separate 'Repeat Diagnostic Testing' blocks: repeat HSAT/PSG/split night requires initial criteria AND at least ONE of 4 conditions; repeat attended titration '(1 and 2 or 3)'; repeat MSLT limited to one repeat by Reimbursement section; frequency cap 'two (2) in 12 months'.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: HSAT meets the definition of medical necessity when all of the following conditions are met (A,B,C,& D)
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Condition B is a negative list ('Absence of ... such as') so 'all' includes a NOT over an open-ended list.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: A full night, attended titration study (95811) meets the definition of medical necessity when the following conditions are met (A &B, A&C, or A&D).
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Group of three alternatives, each AND-ed with A; then the next sentence says APAP is allowed only 'when condition A is met and conditions B, C, and D are not' - so the same four letters drive two opposite decisions.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: A repeat in-lab PAP titration (95811) meets the definition of medical necessity for a member who is known to have OSA when (1 and 2 or 3)
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Precedence of 'and' vs 'or' is not stated; context suggests (1 AND 2) OR 3 but 1 itself contains 'AND any of the following'.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: AHI or RDI or REI measured on HSAT greater than or greater than or equal to 5 events per hour but less than 15

The member was unable to tolerate positive airway pressure therapy following a 1-month minimum trial of APAP as evidenced by the objective data (as noted in the bullet above AND the member did not have a previous attended titration.
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Missing close parenthesis; the final 'AND the member did not have a previous attended titration' might apply to the last bullet only or to all of D.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: at least ONE of the following conditions is met: ... 2. Member has had any of the following • a significant change in weight ... • persistent or recurring signs or symptoms of OSA and adherent with PAP therapy • develop or have a change in cardiovascular status
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Condition 2 is itself an any-of list nested under an at-least-one list.

extraction_hazards: Two-column table layout: test name in left column, criteria in right; pdftotext interleaves, and the criteria text for one block continues after page breaks with the left label missing.

The same 8+6 item comorbidity/sleep-disorder list is copy-pasted 6 times (HSAT B, PSG B/D, titration C, split night B/D, repeat titration 2B/C) with small wording drifts (e.g. 'most days' vs 'most days per week'; truncated bullet 'greater' with text cut: 'opioids on most days per week for greater' then a page break).
Section heading 'Multiple Latency Test (MSLT) Attended Titration' is a garbled label (MSLT is not titration).
Bullets use ○/▪ glyphs and indentation to show nesting; the PDF text loses them in places (e.g. pediatric list nesting).
Criteria are scattered: frequency cap and required documents are in Reimbursement Information; the 'attestation' fallback sits as free-floating notes between tables.
Typos affect logic ('greater than or greater than or equal to 5', missing parenthesis).
LOINC documentation table and long CPT list follow the criteria.
interesting_structures: Same four letters A-D mean different things per test and the combination rule is written in the heading '(A&B, A&C, or D)'.
APAP vs attended titration decided by whether A holds and B, C, D do NOT (a derived negation).
Comorbidity list is used both as a exclusion (HSAT) and an inclusion (PSG): HSAT and PSG are mutually steered by the same facts.
Reimbursement caps (2 in 12 months) and an 'attestation will be accepted' escape hatch when the previous test is not available.
Pediatric branch (<18) with its own indications, HSAT never covered in children.
HGNS pre-implant criteria embedded in a sleep-testing policy (BMI<35, AHI 15-65, CPAP failure definition).

fit_to_tree.why: Logic is all/any/not and mostly numeric, so a tree fits; strain comes from the repeated large exclusion lists, 'such as' open lists, derived negation (APAP when B,C,D absent), hidden frequency caps, and chart facts (PFT results, ABG, PAP download) that are often missing.
